facts.text: Lance Henriksen, star of the 1988 original, was asked to return as Ed Harley but passed after reading the script and finding it "terrible." That's why this sequel has a whole new cast.
Director Jeff Burr first turned the job down because of Puppet Master 4. When original director Tony Randel left after delays, Burr was free and took over.
In this 1958 opening, one of the young greasers is played by John Gatins, who later wrote Flight (2012) and got an Oscar nomination for Best Original Screenplay.
Andrew Robinson (Sheriff Sean Braddock) also played the Scorpio Killer in Dirty Harry and Larry Cotton in Hellraiser. Later he was tailor-spy Garak on Star Trek: Deep Space Nine.
Andrew Robinson, now the lead as Sheriff Sean Braddock, was first set for a supporting part. He got promoted at the last minute when Timothy Bottoms dropped out, per Fangoria.
Soleil Moon Frye, TV's Punky Brewster, had to gain 20 pounds to play Marcie in this film.
Hill Harper (Peter) later became a CSI: NY star. He's also a Harvard Law grad who was a classmate of Barack Obama.
The whole movie was shot in just twenty-four days.
Mayor Bubba is played by Roger Clinton, half-brother of then-President Bill Clinton. Richard Scheib of Moria called it "the most bizarre piece of stunt casting."
Watch Danny swing across the mine on the hook: a safety line is visible several times.
The script had at least four writers and reportedly began life as a non-Pumpkinhead project. Director Jeff Burr admits on the Blu-ray it needed a lot more work.
The script was written by two TV writers who used pseudonyms for their screen credits, according to Fangoria's review of the DVD.
A teen asks "Pet Cemetery?" at the spooky grave, a nod to Stephen King's Pet Sematary (1989).
The Book of the Dead prop from Army of Darkness (1992) sits in Miss Osie's house. KNB Effects worked on both films.
KNB's Greg Nicotero and Gino Crognale studied behind-the-scenes footage of the 1988 original, then built a bulkier Pumpkinhead with more muscle and white eyes. It was practical effects, no CGI.
Richard Scheib of Moria likened Pumpkinhead's role here to Jason Voorhees in Friday the 13th and said the sequel recycles the original with "minimal variation."
Producers made Soleil Moon Frye (Marcie) remove her nose ring after the first day of shooting, which is why it shows up in some scenes and vanishes in others.
Miss Osie's house was built and then burned on Sable Ranch in Santa Clarita. The state had to approve selectively trimming old, protected oak trees first.
A video game, Bloodwings: Pumpkinhead's Revenge, was shot at the same time as the film, sharing sets, actors and props, at producer Jed Weintraub's request.
Judge Dixon's house is the same location used in the 1980 horror comedy Motel Hell.
For quick script tweaks, director Jeff Burr brought back Mark Patrick Carducci and Gary Gerani, the screenwriters of the original 1988 Pumpkinhead.
To dodge an NC-17, director Jeff Burr cut a few seconds of gore, mostly Pumpkinhead clawing up the farmer in the first kill and the monster's own death.
German VHS was trimmed to get an FSK-18 rating. A harsher FSK-16 tape lost over 4 minutes. The uncut film only reached Germany on DVD and Blu-ray in 2017.
Scream queen Linnea Quigley turns up as Nadine in this scene, one of the genre names the video box played up.
R.A. Mihailoff, Leatherface in Jeff Burr's Texas Chainsaw Massacre III, plays Red Byers here. He recalls baring his "hairy ass" for a love scene with Linnea Quigley.
Producer Brad Krevoy co-founded Motion Picture Corporation of America in 1986, a company specializing in low-budget films. It made this sequel and cast well-connected friends in bit parts.
Ami Dolenz (Jenny) had a no-nudity clause. Producers kept pressing for a nude sex scene, so they shot one implying sex and cut away.
Rotten Tomatoes lists only 13% positive out of 8 reviews. Scott Weinberg of DVD Talk gave it 3 of 5 stars, saying the sequel "holds up pretty darn well."
By July 1993, Ami Dolenz and Soleil Moon Frye were shooting extra scenes exclusive to the tie-in PC game Bloodwings: Pumpkinhead's Revenge, whose sets were shared with the film.
Mayor Bubba pitches the monster as tourism: Loch Ness and Bigfoot are "big business." The sheriff reminds him people died, and he replies the town's budget is a tragedy too.
Roger Clinton, who plays the guitar-toting Mayor Bubba, also sings "Just Like You," the film's theme song.
Horror stuntman Kane Hodder plays one of the Knox brothers. The video cover touted him and Linnea Quigley to attract genre fans.
It premiered at the MIFED market in Italy in October 1993. It went direct-to-video in the US on October 19, 1994, and in some territories it was retitled Pumpkinhead: The Demon Returns.
Director Jeff Burr's debut was the anthology From a Whisper to a Scream (1987). He also made Leatherface: Texas Chainsaw Massacre III, which the studio cut heavily.
Actor Mark McCracken, inside the Pumpkinhead suit, recalls plenty of on-set humor. Camcorder footage shows the creature being operated and the gags.
Look closely as Pumpkinhead bursts into the judge's house: the performer's tennis shoes are visible, at least in the fullscreen version.
This is the only Pumpkinhead movie with no appearance by Lance Henriksen's character Ed Harley. The later sequels don't reference its events either.
The 1995 tie-in PC game Bloodwings: Pumpkinhead's Revenge used footage of Ami Dolenz. She says the game is "definitely better" than the movie. PC Gamer US gave it 46%.
The first three Pumpkinhead films all link to Hellraiser: Lance Henriksen, Doug Bradley and Andrew Robinson (Larry Cotton in 1987's Hellraiser) acted in both series.
Behind-the-scenes footage shows Mark McCracken, in the Pumpkinhead suit, repeatedly bumping his head on a ceiling fixture. One giggle fit reportedly got the crew kicked off the set.
